name: solve-js-coding-standards
description: Enforces coding standards, naming conventions, and code structure rules for solve-js
prompt:
You are working on the solve-js project. Follow these coding standards strictly:

## Cardinal Rule: No `any`
Every `any` in production code is a bug. ~15 remain. Zero is the target.

## Error Handling
- NEVER use `throw new Error(...)` in the hot path.
- ALWAYS use typed error factories from @solve-js/errors:
  - `ErrorFactory.parsing(code, message, context?)` for parse failures
  - `ErrorFactory.validation(code, message, context?)` for input limit violations
  - `ErrorFactory.execution(code, message, context?)` for VM runtime errors
  - `ErrorFactory.external(code, message, context?)` for data source failures
  - `ErrorFactory.internal(code, message, context?)` for engine bugs
- NEVER swallow errors silently (the `catch { durMs = 0; }` pattern is a known bug, not a pattern).
- Use `Result<T, E>` type for fallible returns instead of throwing.

## Naming Conventions
- Interfaces: `IPascalCase`
- Type aliases: `PascalCase`
- Enums: `PascalCase`
- Branded types: descriptive suffix (`CurrencyCode`, `VariableName`)
- Functions: `camelCase`, factories use `createX()` or `xValue()`
- Constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`
- One primary export per file, filename matches export name.

## Module Boundaries (strict dependency direction)
- `lexer/` → tokenisation only, no parsing or execution
- `parser/` → AST/bytecode only, no evaluation or I/O
- `vm/` → execution only, no file/network, no imports from parser/lexer
- `engine/` → orchestrates everything, can import from all modules
- `cache/` → storage and retrieval, dependency-free
- `providers/` → domain parselets, no imports from engine/
- `diagnostics/` → event collection, no effect on execution

## Code Structure
- Hard limit: 300 lines per class, 50 lines per function
- Soft limit: 200 lines per class, 30 lines per function
- Nesting depth: hard limit 3 levels
- Every exported symbol gets JSDoc with @param, @returns, @throws
- Use early returns and guard clauses to flatten nesting

## Banned Anti-Patterns
- `new Uint8Array(...)` in hot loops (use buildInto or pool)
- `new Error(...)` in VM (pre-allocate or use SolveError)
- Double-regex matching on same input
- Creating new Lexer per expression (use reset())
- `setTimeout` for async waiting (use waitForCondition())

## TypeScript
- `strict: true` — no exceptions
- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`
- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`
- All `enum` usage `const enum` where possible
- Branded types for domain identifiers
